_about: The single source of truth for every mechanic term. codex is the rule as the player reads it; design.holes is what the mechanic does not do yet. docs/vocabulary.md is generated from this file by tools/export_vocabulary.gd. status: implemented (in sim/), planned (designed, not coded), idea (floated, undecided).

entries.name: Hull
entries.codex: Damage that gets past shield removes hull. Hull never recovers during a battle. At zero the machine is a wreck to be salvaged after the battle.

entries.name: HP
entries.codex: A foe's health. What gets past its armour takes HP off, and at zero the foe falls. A machine's health is its hull.

design.holes: A machine's health is its hull; the engine's code may say either word.

entries.name: Shield
entries.codex: Enemy damage hits shield before hull. A shield absorbs its number: a blow costs it its damage, and whatever it cannot absorb passes to the hull, armour coming off it there; a breaching blow ignores the shield, which stands, and the armour, so the whole blow reaches the hull. Shield components add shield up to the chassis maximum (a component with Overshield may pass it, and the excess fades at the end of the round); in a fight shield comes back only from components, modules and passives. Out of combat it returns each battlefield phase at the chassis's field rate. It never refills for free between skirmishes.

design.holes: Rates and shield sizes are placeholders. No in-combat trickle; a passive may bring one back for one chassis.

entries.name: Heat
entries.codex: Weapons and debuffs may add heat. At the end of your turn, before the enemy acts, heat above the chassis maximum burns hull one for one and the gauge settles at the maximum; until then a vent can still bring it down, and a machine the burn wrecks is lost on its own turn. Vent components remove heat. At the start of every round a machine sheds its chassis's cooling rating in heat, so a round spent on shields or cool weapons is a way of cooling down without a vent. Foes never add heat outright: a Burning machine gains its heat at the end of your turn, just before the overheat, and a Scorched machine's weapons and debuffs run hotter.

design.holes: Heat does nothing below the cap. Consider effects at high heat short of overflow. Cooling numbers are placeholders; cooling must stay below a typical weapon's heat or heat never matters, and a vent component must be worth a whole turn (tuning).

entries.name: Reroll
entries.codex: Three rerolls per round, each rerolling every unlocked, unspent die. A reroll lands on any other component on the die, never the one showing; a second copy of the same component may come up. Rerolls may be spent before or after attacking, so a low damage roll is information for the rest of the round. Never pooled across rounds.

entries.name: Rift Pressure
entries.codex: Ticks once per battlefield phase, never inside a fight. When full it resets and a fresh pack emerges at the rift.

design.holes: It does not escalate yet (section 12's pacing question).

entries.name: Gate Integrity
entries.codex: A pack whose path reaches the gate strikes it instead of moving. Gate integrity persists across battles and is repaired in the meta.

design.holes: The gate damage formula is a placeholder.

entries.name: Weapon
entries.codex: A component that deals damage: spent on a foe within its reach, it deals its number in damage, then its keywords act and its heat lands. One that deals none is equipment. A passive may make another kind a weapon on its machine too (the Whip Scorpion's vents): its hold reads both, Vent, Weapon.

design.holes: The engine's kind is attack for a weapon and a debuff alike: a debuff is an attack of no damage (Face.is_debuff), so code asks is_weapon() for this word and is_attack() for both.

entries.name: Shield component
entries.codex: Spend on self or an ally to add its power in shield, capped at that machine's shield maximum.

entries.name: Vent component
entries.codex: Spend on self or an ally to remove its power in heat.

entries.name: Equipment
entries.codex: A buff or a debuff: a component that deals no damage. A buff is spent on a machine (itself, an ally, or either, as it says) and grants it a status; a debuff is spent on a foe within its reach, its keywords its whole effect. Shields and vents are kinds of their own.

entries.name: Buff component
entries.codex: Equipment spent on a machine (itself, an ally, or either, as the component says) that grants it a status, so many stacks deep, through the end of so many rounds: Overcharged for damage, Armoured against damage, Primed to burn on hit. A status that runs down on its own (Overcharged, halving) takes no rounds. The die shows the status name and the stacks.

entries.name: Damage range
entries.codex: A rolled weapon shows a minimum and a maximum and rolls between them when spent, immediately and visibly. A flat weapon shows one number and never rolls.

entries.name: Direct
entries.codex: Targets any front-rank foe, and any back-rank foe whose column is exposed.

entries.name: Indirect
entries.codex: Targets any foe in either rank, at no cost to its firer.

entries.name: Spread
entries.codex: Player keyword. Also hits the foes in the neighbouring columns of the target's rank, for half the blow.

entries.name: Penetrate
entries.codex: Player keyword. Also hits the other rank of the target's column, for half the blow.

entries.name: Spillover
entries.codex: The Wild Boar's rule, granted to every weapon it fires by its Juggernaut Drive and run by the engine as a keyword: when a blow kills a front-rank foe, what it had past the kill carries into the foe behind it in the same column. Nothing stands behind a massive foe. No component carries it; it becomes a keyword the player learns on its own if a second source ever grants it.

design.holes: The spill is plain damage: it spends a Shock and feeds the Ammit's kill rule, and carries no other keyword of the blow.

entries.name: Cryo
entries.codex: Keyword with a number. Every foe the entry reaches gains that many stacks of Cryo (Cryo 1: one stack). Any machine's hit with a weapon on a foe carrying Cryo spends every stack and cools the hitter 2 a stack.

design.holes: Other pieces may lay it (marked for reuse as a healthier ally cooling than a vent). A rider on the mark is benched until the roster has room. The cooling a stack is a placeholder.

entries.name: Burn
entries.codex: Keyword with a number. On a player's weapon or equipment, Burn 3 means each foe hit gains three stacks of Burning. On a foe's attack the same: each blow that lands leaves that many stacks of Burning on the machine it hit.

design.holes: Its number rides on the face beside the keyword (burn), and the validator asks for it.

entries.name: Lure
entries.codex: Player keyword, on any entry aimed at a foe, a weapon or equipment. Every foe the entry reaches turns on this machine for the round, intents and all; reach and area decide who and how many. A lured foe whose move has no target keeps doing it.

design.holes: No status and no chip: the arrow is the record. A draw by an ally is parked (the bible's redirection row).

entries.name: Shock
entries.codex: Player keyword, on any entry aimed at a foe. Every foe the entry reaches and leaves standing is Shocked: the next blow it takes deals double. The entry's own blow never spends the shock it leaves.

entries.name: Expose
entries.codex: Player keyword, on any entry aimed at a foe. Every foe the entry reaches and leaves standing is Exposed through the next round: in Direct reach of every machine, and its armour counts for nothing. A second Expose refreshes it, never adds.

design.holes: The formation word exposed stays rules text, so the status's id is exposure.

entries.name: Disrupt
entries.codex: Player keyword, on any entry aimed at a foe. The foe does its other move instead, this round, and its new intent shows at once. A foe with nothing else open is not moved.

design.holes: Deterministic: the next move in the foe's list that its conditions allow, so a boss steps through its pattern.

entries.name: Suppress
entries.codex: Player keyword. The target skips its telegraphed action this round, then gains two stacks of Numbed (three if massive). A foe may shrug it off at 10% a Numbed stack; no foe resists by nature.

entries.name: Web
entries.codex: The funnel-web's Web Bomb, locked: the foe hit is Webbed, no damage. After its action the web bursts, Suppressing it and the next foe to act beside it.

design.holes: A keyword, so its chip and checks come free; the burst runs at the end of the foe's action (Skirmish._web_burst).

entries.name: Swap
entries.codex: Player keyword, the Dingo's Combat Translocator's: the spend takes two targets, a foe and then another foe or an empty slot, and the two trade places; no damage. A massive foe does not move. Drag the die to the first, drop it, then tap the second; drag it again to move it or set it back.

entries.name: Flak
entries.codex: Flak N: each foe hit gains N stacks of Flak.

design.holes: The stacks land after the blow, so the blow that lays them never feeds on them and a later strike of the same spend does.

entries.name: Numbed
entries.codex: Foe buff that nothing removes: nothing reads it, deepens it, spreads it, cleanses it or purges it, and nothing that counts a foe's statuses counts it. Each stack is 10% resistance to a suppress, the only resistance a foe has; a suppress it shrugs off does nothing and adds no stack. Loses a stack at the start of each of its turns, so a stun repeated on one foe stops landing while stuns spread across the formation keep working. Its chip wears brackets, the mark of what nothing removes.

design.holes: Its numbers are placeholders, to be judged against fight lengths.

table.stacks: Yes: two a landed suppress, three on a massive foe
table.lasts: A stack fades at each of its turns

entries.name: Paradox
entries.codex: Foe status. While a machine runs the Paradox meter (the Baboon's Pocket Paradox), a foe gains a stack each time it gains any other status: one a spend, however many strikes or stacks. At the machine's count (three) its past self knocks it out: it is Suppressed and the Paradox clears. A foe already suppressed loses its next action instead. Never decays. A status like any other: it counts for what reads a status, and a machine that deepens the statuses it applies deepens it.

design.holes: The count is a placeholder.

table.stacks: Yes: one a debuff gained, a spend; at three it Suppresses and clears

entries.name: Volatile
entries.codex: Keyword with a number, on any kind of component. Volatile 3 means spending it bites its owner for 3 hull, past shield and armour, before the component acts. A blank is never spent, so a disabled entry does not bite.

design.holes: Hull outright, where the Corrupted bite takes shield first. The number is a placeholder.

entries.name: Overcharged a kill
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon (the Soulcutter Talons', locked on the Ammit), with no word of its own: every foe it kills gives its owner so many stacks of Overcharged (two), which the Ammit keeps for the battle.

design.holes: A spread that kills two feeds twice; a chain feeds on every link.

entries.name: Targets
entries.codex: Whom a shield, a vent or a buff may be spent on: self and allies, self only, or allies only. Shown as a chip on the die when narrowed.

entries.name: Chain
entries.codex: If this attack kills an enemy, repeat it on a new, valid target.

entries.name: Rapid
entries.codex: After this component is spent the machine acts again: the die rerolls for free onto any other component (a second copy of this one included, so copies chain). Rapid carries a cooldown of one, so the component is dark for the rest of this round, unless it prints its own cooldown; one that prints none pays heat or hull every spend instead. Any component may carry it, a vent or a shield as well as a weapon.

design.holes: Every Rapid piece carries a limiter (a cooldown, heat or Volatile), which the validator holds content to; a Rapid vent is never below tier three and a Rapid shield never below tier two (the bible's Rapid row).

entries.name: Disable
entries.codex: Enemy keyword. The component the target's die is showing is switched off through the target's next turn: if the die lands on it, it comes up blank.

entries.name: Corrupt
entries.codex: Foe attack keyword with a number. Each blow that lands leaves that many stacks of Corrupted on the component the target's die is showing (Corrupt 2: two): it deals damage to its owner whenever spent, a bite a stack.

entries.name: Silence
entries.codex: Foe keyword, on a blow or as a move of its own. The machine it lands on is Silenced: its buffs count for nothing and its components' keywords are muted through its next round. A Ward turns it away.

design.holes: Who carries it is section 12's question. Cast only where a machine carries a buff (the move's machine_buffed condition), aimed at the buffed; it touches no store.

entries.name: Purge
entries.codex: Foe keyword, a hero's or a boss's, on a blow or as a move of its own. The machine it lands on loses every buff it carries (a kept Overcharged too), every stack; its stores and its passives stay. A Ward turns it away.

design.holes: Who carries it is section 12's question. The id stays dispel. It takes no store; a store's active effect, when one exists, is silenced for a turn instead, since the store would grant it again.

entries.name: Cleanse
entries.codex: Player keyword, on shield and vent components. Whoever the component is spent on also loses every Burning, Scorched, Silenced, Disabled and Corrupted status. A rapid component's own switch-off is not a status a cleanse touches.

entries.name: Overshield
entries.codex: Player keyword, on shield components, rare. The shield may raise its target past the target's maximum; shield past the maximum fades at the end of the round. A shield die spent on a machine already at its maximum is never wasted when it carries this.

design.holes: Rare because every overshield on the field makes shield max a soft number; the fade is the whole safeguard, since a lasting excess would stack a team past every blow.

entries.name: Retaliate
entries.codex: Machine status. While it lasts, a foe that strikes this machine's bare hull is Shocked. It lasts the rounds the component that grants it says.

table.stacks: No: one does all it does

entries.name: Shocked
entries.codex: Foe status. The next blow of a weapon this foe takes deals double damage, then the status clears; equipment (a lure, a probe) leaves it standing. Never stacks. Laid by the Shock keyword, and on a foe that strikes the bare hull of a machine carrying Retaliate.

table.stacks: Never
table.lasts: Until the next team blow of a weapon

entries.name: Exposed
entries.codex: Foe status. In Direct reach of every machine as if its column's front were empty, and its armour counts for nothing, its own and any Armoured. Through the next round; refreshed, never added. A back-rank foe whose front is empty is exposed by its formation, in reach only.

design.holes: The id is exposure, since exposed names the formation word and the foes' default aim.

table.stacks: Never: a second Expose refreshes it

entries.name: Syrinx Drone
entries.codex: Foe status, the Lammergeier's: the next weapon to kill it, any machine's, leaves its shot in the slot it empties, a mine. One mine a drone; it lasts the fight, and a death by a tick leaves nothing.

design.holes: A status the team put on the foe, so the Paradox counts it.

table.stacks: Never: one drone at a time
table.lasts: The fight, until a weapon kills it

entries.name: Overcharged
entries.codex: Machine status. Each stack is +1 damage on this machine's attacks, flat, so the count is the bonus. At the end of each round it halves, rounded down, whatever granted it, until it is gone. On the Ammit nothing of it fades: its Quintessence Tap keeps every stack for the battle.

design.holes: Every grant is one status on the machine and the stacks add up. A halving rule has no duration, so a buff component grants stacks and no rounds. The name is a placeholder.

table.stacks: Yes: a damage point a stack
table.lasts: Halves at the end of each round, rounded down, until gone; on the Ammit the battle, nothing fading

entries.name: Sealed
entries.codex: Machine status, the Armadillo's form. A shield it spends on itself seals it: armour up by its Lockdown's number, its own cooling stopped, and it runs hotter at the end of each turn. A vent or a weapon opens it; a shield on an ally and equipment leave it as it is. An ally's vent still cools it.

design.holes: One chip, renewing, never stacking: the armour it grants is tied to the form. The numbers are placeholders.

table.stacks: Renews: one seal however many shields
table.lasts: Until a vent or a weapon opens it, or the skirmish ends

entries.name: Cryo
entries.codex: Foe status, the mark the Cryo keyword leaves. Any machine's hit on it with a weapon spends every stack and cools the hitter 2 a stack; equipment spends none. It never fades on its own.

design.holes: Engine id cryoed, since the keyword holds cryo; the player reads Cryo on both.

table.stacks: Yes: the Cryo's number per foe reached; a weapon's hit spends every stack
table.lasts: Until a weapon's hit spends it, or the skirmish ends

entries.name: Armoured
entries.codex: Status, on either side. Armour +1 a stack: that much off every blow that reaches it, flat, every stack at once, whatever granted it, so the count is the armour. On a machine (a buff, an armouring component, a passive) it lasts until the round's end and comes off blows on bare hull; on a foe, from its brace, it lasts until its next action.

design.holes: The engine id stays braced.

table.stacks: Yes: an armour point a stack, every stack going at once
table.lasts: A machine's until the round's end; a foe's until its next action

entries.name: Primed
entries.codex: Machine status. Every blow this machine lands leaves a stack of Burning per stack of Primed. Granted by a buff for the rounds it says.

design.holes: A placeholder name.

table.stacks: Yes: a Burning stack a blow per stack

entries.name: Disabled
entries.codex: Component status. This die entry comes up blank while it lasts; the component itself is untouched. A foe's disable lasts through the machine's next turn and can be cleansed; a rapid component's own switch-off ends with the round.

table.stacks: No

entries.name: Corrupted
entries.codex: Component status. Every time this die entry is spent it bites its owner for 3 per stack, shield first, before the component acts. A blank is never spent, so a disabled entry does not bite. Stacks. Clears at end of skirmish. Can be cleansed.

design.holes: The bite is the status's own number in the engine's table, a placeholder.

table.stacks: Yes: its bite a stack

entries.name: Phased
entries.codex: Machine status. It cannot act, take damage or be targeted until the round's end. Granted only to a machine that has not acted this round.

design.holes: Not targetable means allies cannot vent or shield it either, and a foe's intent on it picks again; it still cools by its own cooling, and ticks and overheats still land. Aphelion's pieces may grant it beside the Swallowtail's screens.

table.stacks: No

entries.name: Burning
entries.codex: Status. On a foe: loses 1 HP per stack at the start of its action, then loses one stack; bypasses armour. On a machine: gains 1 heat per stack at the end of the player's turn, before the overheat, then loses one stack, so a vent makes room for it or a cleanse takes it off. Metal does not burn, it heats.

design.holes: Engine ids burning (a foe's) and burning_mech (a machine's).

table.stacks: Yes: the Burn's number per blow, or as many as the foe's move says
table.lasts: Until the stacks run out: one fades at each tick (a foe's action; the end of the player's turn on a machine)

entries.name: Suppressed
entries.codex: Foe status. Skips its action this round, then clears.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: One action: this round's, or the next if it has acted

entries.name: Vitriol
entries.codex: Foe status, the funnel-web's acid. At its action it loses 10% of its current HP a stack, past armour, after Burning, rounded down, then a stack fades. A share of what is left: it opens on a boss and never finishes a foe.

design.holes: Only the funnel-web's passive lays it; a keyword that ever carries it shares the word. Whether a tick passes Guarded is the parts' question, as Burning's is. The word Corroded is kept for a foe's damage over time on machines.

table.stacks: Yes: a stack per weapon hit on a foe showing no intent on the spider; a tick a stack
table.lasts: A stack fades at each of its actions

entries.name: Webbed
entries.codex: Foe status, the funnel-web's web. At the end of its action the web bursts: it and the next foe to act beside it are Suppressed, Numbed resisting each for itself. Killed first, it takes its web with it; one the team has already suppressed gains nothing from the burst on itself.

design.holes: The burst catches the next foe to act beside it in its rank, the one to its left when none stands to its right; on a foe already suppressed it is wasted, and each half feeds the Paradox as the Suppress keyword's does.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: Until the end of its action this round, when it bursts

entries.name: Spun Up
entries.codex: Machine status, the Cassowary's. Its next spend at a foe deals 2 more a stack, then every stack is spent: a weapon's blow takes them, a debuff spends them for nothing. Carried between turns until then.

design.holes: Spent whole by the next spend at a foe, a weapon's or a debuff's.

table.stacks: Yes: its bonus a stack, every stack spent by the next spend at a foe
table.lasts: Until its next spend at a foe, across turns

entries.name: Hot Streak
entries.codex: Machine status, the Kite's: its shots run 1 hotter a stack this fight, a stack for each attack that killed. Its passive's price: no cleanse, silence or purge lifts it.

design.holes: A working name, the Kite's heat tax.

table.stacks: Yes: one for each attack that killed

entries.name: Shots
entries.codex: Machine count, the Cassowary's: its spends at foes this fight, a weapon's or a debuff's, shown as six pips under the heat bar, the sixth lit when it is next, where its sixth shot counts double. Shields, vents, buffs and spins are no shots. Never a chip; nothing cleanses it; it resets each fight.

design.holes: Kept only for a machine whose rule counts (an nth_shot condition).

table.stacks: Yes: one a spend at a foe

entries.name: Quick turn spent
entries.codex: Machine marker, the Needletail's gate: its free setup this round is spent, so its next debuff or buff this round is a full action. Never a chip: the die shows the gate open by the Rapid it grants a setup. Gone at the round's end.

design.holes: Set by a static grant of Rapid on setup_once (the Needletail's relay).

table.stacks: No

entries.name: Siphoning
entries.codex: Machine status, the Whip Scorpion's Siphon: every blow a foe lands on it this round adds heat, 2 a blow, whatever the blow dealt. The blows land in the enemy's turn, after the overheat, so it is next round's fuel for its vents, or next turn's burn. Until the round's end; nothing cleanses it.

design.holes: The number is the entry's own (heat_per_blow), the lever.

table.stacks: No: its entry's heat a blow

entries.name: Flak
entries.codex: Foe status, Wainwright & Sutler's on-hit. Every blow of a weapon it takes deals a point more a stack. At the end of each round the stacks halve, rounded down.

design.holes: Adds before multiplies and before armour, to a weapon's blow of 0 too (Ryan, 25 October: "Flak and overcharge exist in part to get past armour"), so a Shocked foe carrying Flak takes blow plus Flak, doubled. The id follows the participle habit (Burning, Webbed). Numbers are placeholders; Flak beside Overcharged at a point a stack each may read too strong, the two read together on the Prairie Dog's rows.

table.stacks: Yes: N a hit from a Flak N piece; a point more on every blow of a weapon it takes, a stack
table.lasts: Halves at the end of each round, rounded down, until gone

entries.name: Cracked component
entries.codex: Machine status, global rule. When what one blow puts on the hull, past shield and armour, is at least a quarter of maximum hull, the machine's die is rolled and the component it lands on is injured. An intact component cracks: it loses its keywords and unique effects, but still does its basic action, still generates heat, keeps any cooldown it prints, and still provides its passive bonuses and abilities. A shield prevents an injury only by absorbing enough of the blow, and a blow a Barrier takes never injures. A cracked component stays cracked across skirmishes and battles until repaired in the hangar.

design.holes: The threshold is a placeholder. Repair cost and the hangar screen are not built.

entries.name: Destroyed component
entries.codex: Machine status. When an injury lands on a component that is already cracked, it is destroyed: blank, it does nothing when it comes up, and provides its passive bonuses but not passive abilities, until the hangar repairs or replaces it. An injury that lands on a destroyed component or an empty hardpoint finds nothing to break, so a badly broken machine shrugs off more of them.

entries.name: Front rank
entries.codex: Four slots, one a column. Front-rank foes fill these. Always in Direct reach.

entries.name: Back rank
entries.codex: Four slots behind the front. Back-rank foes hold these.

entries.name: Exposed
entries.codex: A back-rank foe is exposed when the front slot in its column is empty. Exposed foes are in Direct reach.

entries.name: Mine
entries.codex: A shot waiting in an empty slot of the enemy's formation: laid there by a machine whose weapons and equipment aimed at foes may also be spent on an empty slot (the Lammergeier's Fuse-delayed Bay), as if a foe stood there, or left by a kill on a foe carrying the Syrinx Drone. Its number is fixed when laid and its keywords ride in it; the shots in one slot stack. Whoever steps into the slot takes every shot waiting, in laid order, before it acts (a massive foe both slots'), through its own armour and statuses; every keyword acts as on a blow, and Lure and Disrupt do nothing, their round being over. Any way in sets it off, and nothing expires.

design.holes: The landing waits until the reinforcement step has placed every arrival, then goes left to right, so a Spread mine catches the arrivals beside it. A Swap that moves a foe into a mined slot sets it off at once.

entries.name: Reinforcements
entries.codex: Foes not yet on the field. Front and Back ranks have their own reinforcement pool. Empty slots refill from the pool of reinforcements after each round. The skirmish is won when the field and all reinforcements are defeated.

design.holes: How elites arrive is section 12's question.

entries.name: Massive
entries.codex: A massive foe fills both slots of a column and counts as front rank. Its column is never exposed while it stands. Only some elites and bosses are massive.

design.holes: Spread treats it as a front-rank neighbour; Penetrate finds nothing behind it.

entries.name: Withdraw
entries.codex: Available at any point of the player's turn, the first round included. The price is always the same: your turn ends (heat over the maximum burns), the enemy takes its full turn, then the skirmish ends, so nobody leapfrogs out of contact unscathed. Machines keep their damage; a pack keeps its survivors, who return whole. Shields do not refill on withdrawing; they recharge at the field rate only in phases spent out of combat.

entries.name: Movespeed
entries.codex: Move in tens: how far a machine goes in an action. A normal hex costs 10, so MOVE 40 is four hexes on open ground. Each way of moving calls each ground fast (5), normal (10) or slow: a slow hex can always be entered with any move left, and the step ends the move. Move left at the end of a phase is lost.

design.holes: Every chassis's move is a placeholder set by size and role; the content check flags a chassis at least as fast as another on every ground, never refuses it.

entries.name: Walk
entries.codex: The map shows where every pack will walk on the enemy's turn, worked out from where your machines stand now: a pusher toward the gate, a hunter toward its prey. Packs go round your machines; nothing you do stops one, and nothing a pack does reacts to your plan.

design.holes: A pack with no way to the gate waits, and the map says so.

entries.name: Fight
entries.codex: Tap a pack to attack it. The fight is at that pack's hex: every pack whose ring covers it joins, and you commit the machines whose attack range covers it. One fight at a time, each resolved before the next; a machine that fought, won, lost or withdrew, is spent until your next turn.

entries.name: Spent
entries.codex: A machine that has fought this turn is spent: it cannot move or fight again until your next turn. A machine whose passive grants a second action has two before it is spent.

entries.name: Carry
entries.codex: A machine that carries (the Swallowtail's Muster Deck) lifts the machines on the hexes beside it when it moves: they travel as a ring round it and land as a block, each where it rode from it, keeping whatever move and action they had. It cannot stop where a rider would land on a hex it cannot stand on (NO ROOM). A caught machine does not ride.

design.holes: A landing animation or a redistribution on landing may come later.

entries.name: Caught
entries.codex: A machine a hunter has caught fights it first on your turn, before any other fight, and cannot move until then. Others in range may join that fight. Withdrawing ends it, and the hunter catches the machine again while it lives.

entries.name: Ring
entries.codex: Every unit has a ring. A pack's ring is who it supports: a pack whose ring covers the pack you attack joins the fight. A hunter's ring is how close it must be to catch its prey. A machine's ring is its attack range, two hexes: it can join a fight whose target is that close.

design.holes: Rings are content on the foe type, placeholders; a machine's attack range is two for every chassis, an exception only where a role earns it.

entries.name: Behaviour
entries.codex: A pusher walks toward the gate and threatens nothing else. A hunter locks one machine, by its caveat (the nearest, weakest, strongest or slowest), wears the target rings on it and walks toward it; when it ends its walk with its prey inside its ring it has caught it, and that fight comes first on your next turn. A caught machine cannot move until the fight, and is caught again while the hunter lives.

design.holes: Push and hunt are the only behaviours; the hunters' caveats are placeholders.

entries.name: Pack
entries.codex: An enemy hex is a pack: one foe type times a strength. A fight is the pack you attack and every pack whose ring covers it, so the rift's formations and the order you attack them in decide what you fight. A boss is one unit on one hex.

design.holes: The rift should spawn formations, not single packs: the foes' fresh start.

entries.name: Footprint
entries.codex: Every unit covers one hex, the boss included: it is occupied, counts for rings and range, and is a tap target. The gate and the rift are wider structures.

design.holes: Footprints do not rotate with facing.

entries.name: Structure
entries.codex: Gate and rift hexes are structures wider than one hex. Nobody stands on them. A pack that ends its walk beside a gate hex strikes the gate.

design.holes: The rift does nothing yet beyond marking where packs spawn.

entries.name: Spawn
entries.codex: When Rift Pressure fills, the next pack of the spawn cycle (the lead domain's packs alternating with the guest's) appears on the nearest free hex to the rift.

design.holes: A full spawn list should arrive together as a formation; pressure currently sends one pack at a time.

entries.name: Plain
entries.codex: Open ground. Normal pace for every machine; wheels run fast. Packs cross it.

entries.name: Road
entries.codex: Open ground, the same as plain: the road is art. Normal pace for every machine; wheels run fast. Packs cross it.

entries.name: Rough
entries.codex: Forest and scrub. Normal pace for tracks, walkers and flyers; slow for wheels and hovercraft, which can enter it but end their move there. Packs cross it at full pace.

entries.name: Ruins
entries.codex: Rubble. Normal pace for walkers and flyers; slow for tracks, wheels and hovercraft, which can enter it but end their move there. Packs cross it at full pace.

design.holes: No skirmish condition yet; what terrain does in a fight is section 12's question.

entries.name: Water
entries.codex: Hovercraft skim it fast and tracks ford at normal pace; walkers and wheels can enter it but end their move there; flyers pass over. Packs never enter it.

design.holes: No skirmish condition yet (section 12). The generator gives every map one real water feature with crossings for the horde.

entries.name: Mountain
entries.codex: Impassable except for flyers, which cross at normal pace. Packs go around.

entries.name: Flyer
entries.codex: Normal pace over every ground, mountains included. Packs walk under it but never stop on its hex.

entries.name: Hover
entries.codex: Skims water fast. Rough ground and ruins are slow: it can enter them, and the step ends its move.

entries.name: Walker
entries.codex: Legs. Rough ground and ruins at normal pace; water is slow: it can enter it, and the step ends its move.

entries.name: Tracked
entries.codex: Tracks. Ploughs through forest and fords water at normal pace; rubble is slow: it can enter ruins, and the step ends its move.

entries.name: Wheeled
entries.codex: Wheels. Fast on open ground. Rough ground, ruins and water are slow: it can enter them, and the step ends its move.

entries.name: City defense
entries.codex: A static player-side unit. Not on the field yet.

design.holes: No die and no rule yet: how gate defences work is section 12's question.

entries.name: On attack
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires after the damage roll on every attack. Effects: multiply or add damage or heat, multiply the printed number alone before any buff (the Kite's double), or set a minimum damage. An effect may carry a when condition: component_cracked (only when the component being spent is cracked).

entries.name: On shield gain
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine gains shield from any source, with the amount gained; it may shed heat or grant a status, never raise more shield.

design.holes: No content uses it yet.

entries.name: On shielding an ally
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine spends a shield component on an ally, with the shield's size; it may shed the ally's heat or grant the ally a status, never raise more shield. It never fires for a shield on itself.

design.holes: Fires on the spend, whatever the shield gained, so a shield die on a topped-up ally still does its other work.

entries.name: On heat gain
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine gains heat, with the amount; it may raise shield or grant a status, never add heat.

entries.name: On round start
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires after the roll, before rerolls: shield from heat, a flat shield, a vent.

design.holes: The heat it reads is the gauge after the turn's passive cooling (the Buzzard's Thermal Recoupler).

entries.name: On skirmish start
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires once as the skirmish begins, before the first roll: a shield, a vent, a status.

design.holes: No content uses it yet.

entries.name: On foe status
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when any foe gains a status, whoever applied it: once for each status a spend puts on a foe, however many strikes or stacks (an application, not a stack). Never for Paradox, nor for the Suppressed a Paradox causes, and Numbed is no status. Effects: paradox (the foe gains a stack of Paradox; at the count it is Suppressed and the Paradox clears).

entries.name: On applying stacks
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine applies stacks of a status to anyone: a foe's Burning (from a burn or from Primed), an ally's or its own buff, its own Overcharged from a kill. Effects: add_stacks (so many stacks more, flat or for every so much heat the machine carries). Never for Numbed, which is exempt from every interaction.

design.holes: Shocked and Suppressed are not stacks, so it never touches them.

entries.name: On hull damage
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when this machine loses hull: to a blow, a bite or an overheat.

design.holes: The hook for the pinned berserker idea too.

entries.name: On a kill
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires once after an attack of this machine's that killed, however many foes fell to it, chains, spills and a vent's blast included: a status (the Kite's Hot Streak), a shield or a vent.

entries.name: Out of combat
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires at the end of a battlefield phase in which this machine had no skirmish, after the field recharge: more shield.

design.holes: Heat does not persist between fights, so a vent here would be nothing. No content uses it yet.

entries.name: Command die
entries.codex: One die rolled alongside the machines' dice each round. Its entries are rechargeable commander abilities and never deal damage. They come from the hangar, never from rewards. Die size is a research path.

design.holes: Open question: whether the command die exists at all, or one-shots only.

entries.name: One-shot
entries.codex: Consumable ability. A pouch of three: a fourth forces a use or a discard. One comes from a Fracture's pick, and a starting stock chosen in the hangar restocks every battle. It expires when the rift closes.

entries.name: Reward pick
entries.codex: Each Fracture of the Rupture meter grants one, unweighted by domain: one of three, a battle-long modifier on a component you carry, a one-shot, or a battle-wide boon (an extra reroll a round).

entries.name: City ability
entries.codex: Battlefield-level ability owned and upgraded by the city: sprint, airlift, teleport, tractor beam, orbital strike. Cooldowns measured in phases.

design.holes: Consider range limits from the gate so the push north leaves support behind.

entries.name: Cooldown
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component: once spent, its entry goes dark for that many rounds, this one included, and the die shows it dark with the turns left; the die can still land on it, and nothing in it acts. Rapid carries a cooldown of one unless the component prints its own, and "no cooldown" lifts even that. No cleanse lifts a cooldown, and a crack keeps it.

design.holes: A crack keeps it, a price as heat is. The city's battlefield abilities count their own cooldowns in phases.

entries.name: Reset
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon: if its spend kills, every entry dark from a cooldown comes back, itself included, and its machine acts again, the free roll never landing on the entry just spent; a team reroll may bring it back up, and every kill resets it again (the Kite's Pinion Driver).

design.holes: No limit (Ryan, 24 October: "Let the Kite reset infinitely. There are other ways to nerf it that aren't more rules exceptions"): the free roll never lands on the entry just spent, so each action past the second is a team reroll back onto it and another kill, and the Kite's heat climbs with every kill.

entries.name: Pull
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component (the Lammergeier's Lorentz Contractor, a debuff): every mine on the field gathers into the slot it is spent on, in laid order, and a foe standing there takes them now. Spent on an empty slot, it gathers them there.

design.holes: Never Rapid, so a pull costs the turn and the laying is still chosen.

entries.name: Drone
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component (the Lammergeier's Syrinx Drone, a debuff): the foe carries the Syrinx Drone. If it already carries Exposed, the spend is Rapid; otherwise it gives the foe Exposed, never refreshing it.

design.holes: The condition is read before the drone lands, so its own Exposed never makes it Rapid.

entries.name: Spray
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon (the Skua's Flechette Pod): its first strike lands on the foe it is spent on, and each strike after it falls on a random foe in reach at that moment, the same foe again allowed. A kill clears its slot at once, so a hole burnt in the front rank opens the foe behind it to the strikes still to come.

design.holes: The die shows the first strike's number, as a Spread does (Ryan, 17 October); a later strike may spend a Shock on another foe, an understood risk ("no different than using a cleave").

entries.name: Component
entries.codex: A piece of kit on a machine, and one entry on its die. There is no generic kit: every entry on a die is a component, or an empty hardpoint. Each round the die is rolled and the component that comes up is what the machine can do.

design.holes: Multi-slot components were set aside as invisible complexity.

entries.name: Hardpoint
entries.codex: A free slot on the chassis. Any component fits any hardpoint. On the model a hardpoint is a socket where the component mounts.

entries.name: Fixed component
entries.codex: A component built into the chassis: always on the die, never removed, never sold, and it uses no hardpoint. It is the machine's own: no other machine carries one, and it can never be built.

design.holes: Never bought open. Locked pieces are powerful and unique, never blueprints, so no hardpoint stocks one and none carries a tier (the validator holds it; ContentDB.component_tier answers 0).

entries.name: Empty hardpoint
entries.codex: A hardpoint with nothing in it is an entry on the die that does nothing when it comes up. Nothing fills it for you.

entries.name: Module
entries.codex: Kit inside the machine, not on its die: a few numbers up or down, and at most one rule of its own. A chassis has its module slots (two, three on the Clydesdale), and a module is never spent: it is always working.

design.holes: Fitted in the harness only: the campaign's roster, the loot that drops them and the hangar wait for the economy pass and the hangar screen.

entries.name: On injury
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Fires when an injury lands on a component. Effects: no_destroy (a cracked component holds instead of being destroyed).

entries.name: Armour
entries.codex: A chassis number taken off every blow that reaches the hull, flat, never a percentage: a blow on bare hull and what passes a shield alike, never a breach, which ignores it. A blow at or under the armour does nothing to the hull. Shield is not armoured: a blow on shield costs the shield its full damage.

design.holes: Numbers are placeholders.

entries.name: Strike order
entries.codex: Foes strike in the order they stand: front rank left to right, then the back rank. Each blow is resolved on its own against the shield standing at that moment, so which foe strikes first decides what a small shield blocks. At first contact the heaviest hitters deploy left.

entries.name: Aim
entries.codex: Whom a foe strikes, picked for every foe on its own as the round opens and shown as its arrow before you act: at random, unless the foe carries an aim. The foes never pile onto a machine their blows would already wreck while another stands. The exposed: weighted toward the machine its blow would hurt most, a shield standing lowering the draw and a shield about to break raising it. Anything: any machine alike. Heat: the hottest machine. The armed: a machine showing an intact weapon or debuff. Fires as one: the rank shares a pick. A move may aim differently from its foe. The pick is a commitment: a foe whose target shields up still swings at it.

design.holes: Content: aim on a foe type and on a move; when on a move is the condition that lets a foe pick it, and a special never fires twice running.

entries.name: Breach
entries.codex: A breaching blow ignores the shield and the armour: the shield stands, the armour counts for nothing, and the whole blow lands. On a foe's move it reaches a machine's hull, and if what gets through is a quarter of maximum hull it injures a component; a Ward turns it away, and the shield and armour then take the blow like any other. On a weapon it ignores a foe's armour.

entries.name: Self-Destruct
entries.codex: A blow that spends the striker: after it lands the foe is gone, whole, and nothing brings it back. The blow is the foe's whole life, so it is announced like any other and the answer is to kill it first or to shield what it has picked.

design.holes: A property of a foe's attack action, like breach. A self-destructing foe counts as a kill like any other.

entries.name: Every Machine
entries.codex: A blow at every machine: each of its strikes lands on every machine in the fight in turn, so no aim and no lure moves it, and the number shown is what each machine takes. A shield saves only the machine it stands on; the answers that stop the whole blow are aimed at the striker: kill it, suppress it, disrupt it.

design.holes: A property of a foe's attack action. Its number is per machine, so a move with it is priced well under a single blow from the same foe. The name is a working one.

entries.name: Last Act
entries.codex: A blow a foe lands the moment it falls, shown on it by the skull and its number. It lands at once, before anything else, even when the foe was the last one standing, so shield up before the kill rather than after.

design.holes: Content: on_death.blow, an attack's shape (name, factor, strikes, keywords), beside or instead of a split. No foe carries it yet.

entries.name: Parts
entries.codex: A foe in parts: a core and the parts that stand with it. While its parts stand (all of them, or any, by the foe) the core is Guarded and takes no damage; a fallen part may grow back after a few rounds; when the core falls, its parts fall with it. Choose what to focus: a part to open the core, or the core to end them all.

design.holes: Content: parts (foe ids), guard (all or any), regrow_parts (rounds). Parts are found by pack and type, one deep, and deploy by the ordinary rules, so beside the core is likely but not placed. No foe carries it yet.

entries.name: Countdown
entries.codex: A move that gathers before it lands: announced as the round opens, it lands the stated number of rounds later, its warning chip counting down the whole time. Nothing hits while it gathers. Suppress holds it a round, Disrupt breaks it off, and killing the foe ends it.

design.holes: The foe stays on the field while it gathers; its pick holds while the machine stands, and a Lure moves it.

entries.name: Foe action
entries.codex: A foe has a base attack, the quick read of how hard it hits, and a list of actions: attacks that scale it, and defends, buffs and debuffs it does instead of a blow (bracing against damage, regrowing or curing one of its own, readying to get back up, calling up a foe, rallying the others, costing the team a reroll, setting a machine burning, switching off the entry a die shows, scorching or corrupting every machine). Each round every foe on the field picks one by weight before the player acts, so what it will do and to whom is announced exactly. An attack's damage is the base times its factor, and the help text shows the resulting number.

design.holes: A foe's whole brain is its weighted draw and its aim; none plans ahead.

entries.name: Vents all
entries.codex: An attack that fires the machine's whole heat as it is spent: the heat gauge is empty after the shot, and every step of heat fired, the step printed on the entry, adds the component's bonus to the blow before the passives. The shot's own heat cost still lands.

design.holes: Only the first shot of a chain fires the heat.

entries.name: Grows with missing HP
entries.codex: A flat blow that grows with its target's lost HP: it adds its bonus for every step of HP the target is missing, both numbers printed on the entry, read as the die is spent. No roll is involved, so the number is known before the spend, and the die shows it while held over a target.

design.holes: Both numbers are the entry's own (power_per_missing and per_missing), placeholders.

entries.name: Gated
entries.codex: A keyword printed with a condition, such as a Suppress on a foe carrying Flak or on a foe carrying two Burning or more: it lands only on a foe that meets the condition, read as the die is spent and before the blow's own riders, so a spend never opens its own gate. Held over a foe where the condition does not hold, the die shows the keyword's chip struck through.

design.holes: Suppress alone carries a gate today. A working name for Ryan's name pass.

entries.name: Consumes
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon: its blow consumes every stack of the status it names on its target and deals a point more for each stack consumed, before the multiplies. The die held over the foe shows the number with the stacks in.

design.holes: A mine laid from it eats its arrival's stacks.

entries.name: Burns its firer
entries.codex: A rule printed on a weapon: spending it sets its own machine Burning, the stacks it says, after the blow. The machine's Burning heats it at the end of the player's turn, before the overheat, then loses a stack, so a vent makes room for it and a cleanse takes it off. Fuel for a machine that wants heat, a price for one that does not.

design.holes: A working name for Ryan's name pass.

entries.name: The hopper
entries.codex: Two weapons that work together. One fills its machine's hopper, a load for each foe its blows reach, after the blow. The other fires the hopper: each load it takes adds its bonus to the blow, up to its most a shot, and the loads it takes are spent. The hopper lasts the skirmish and shows on the machine; the die shows what a shot would fire.

design.holes: The numbers are placeholders; the Honey Badger's rework (its brief) may change the fill.

entries.name: Braces
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component (the Breaching Plow's). Spending it Armours its owner, the stacks it says (an armour point each), until the round's end: the armour stands behind the blow through the enemy's turn.

design.holes: A rule on one carrier, not a keyword, until another piece wants it; the stacks are a placeholder.

entries.name: Rolls again
entries.codex: A rule printed on a component (the Nemesis's Knuckle of Fury). Spending it with a stack of the status it names spends one, and the die rolls again, a plain roll as the round opens, so the machine acts again and the same component may show again. Unlike Rapid nothing switches off: the stacks are the limit.

design.holes: A rule on one carrier, not a keyword, until another piece wants it.

entries.name: Strikes
entries.codex: An attack's blows per use. A weapon with three strikes lands three separate hits: each rolls its own damage and carries its own effects, so a rapid-fire weapon procs often (the Skua's strikes share each roll, halved). Against a shield, each strike is its own blow, so once one breaks the shield the next reaches the hull; against armour, every small strike loses the armour, so many small hits are the wrong tool for a heavy target and the right one for a soft one. Foe attacks have strikes too.

design.holes: Heat is paid once per use, not per strike.

entries.name: Static
entries.codex: Passive trigger. Always on. Its effects change a machine's numbers or a component's properties while a condition holds, rather than firing on an event: add_stat and multiply_stat on hull, shield, heat, armour, move or recharge; add_damage_taken and multiply_damage_taken on every incoming blow; weapon_cooldown (every weapon the machine fires goes dark for so many rounds: the Kite's); set_reach on a component (direct or indirect while a condition holds); suppress, which turns off another effect by id or tag.

design.holes: Every read asks the pipeline; nothing is written to a stat or a component, so an effect that is gone stops answering. A static reach rule cannot be conditioned on reach.

entries.name: Order of operations
entries.codex: Everything that changes a number goes through one pipeline, in one order. Sources: the chassis passive and each fitted component's passive (until refitted), skirmish rewards (until the battle ends), buffs and debuffs (until the skirmish ends, or until the end of a given round). First suppression, shortest-lived source to longest: a live effect that suppresses another by id or tag turns it off, and a suppressed effect suppresses nothing. Then the gate: an effect takes part only if it is live, its trigger fires now, its condition holds, and, for an ability, its component is not destroyed (a destroyed component keeps its stat bonuses and loses its abilities). Then adds, all sources summed; then multiplies, all sources multiplied; then floors and caps; then overrides, where the shortest-lived source wins and the latest granted breaks ties. In an attack, the roll (or the flat number, with what fired heat or a target's missing hull adds) comes before the pipeline's adds and multiplies; a raised ceiling or floor moves a rolled range before the roll, and the die shows it. Nothing is ever stored as a total: every read asks again, so an effect that is gone stops answering. Statuses stack: the same status granted again adds stacks instead of a second copy; an add is worth its value per stack and a multiply is applied once per stack; a status that ticks applies its per-stack tick at its owner's turn, then loses one stack, and is gone at zero.

design.holes: Refit (the hangar) is what changes loadout-scoped effects; not built.

entries.name: Rage
entries.codex: Machine store, the Nemesis's: a rage for every time it takes hull damage (a blow, a bite of its own, an overheat), up to 5, kept for the skirmish. Its fists spend one when they strike, and the die rolls again. Never decays; no cleanse, Silence or Purge touches it.

design.holes: Capped at 5 (the passive's stack_status cap).

table.stacks: Yes: one a hull hit, up to 5; one spent a fist

entries.name: Hopper
entries.codex: Machine store, the Honey Badger's: loads its Chainsaw Claw digs out of whatever it hits, which its Bullion Fragmenter fires a few a shot. Lasts the skirmish; never decays, and no cleanse, Silence or Purge touches it.

design.holes: No cap and no grant yet: the Honey Badger's rework (its brief) gives it a cap and an armour a load; today it shows as a chip.

table.stacks: Yes: a load a foe the claw reaches, up to three spent a shot

entries.name: Scorched
entries.codex: Machine status, from a foe's scorch: every weapon and debuff it fires runs 1 hotter per stack, until the end of the player's turn, when every stack goes. Spending a shield, a vent, a buff or a cool weapon plays round it. Can be cleansed.

design.holes: Placeholder numbers.

table.stacks: Yes: its heat a stack
table.lasts: Until the end of the player's turn, every stack at once

entries.name: Kindled
entries.codex: Foe status, from a rally. It hits harder by its rally's value through the next round. It goes live when that round's intents are drawn, so a foe striking after the rallier this turn hits the number it showed.

table.stacks: Yes: each rally's value adds

entries.name: Getting Back Up
entries.codex: Foe status, from a Reraise, its own or an ally's. After it falls it returns to the reinforcements once, whole, unless it self-destructed.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: Until it falls; it returns once

entries.name: Silenced
entries.codex: Machine status, from a foe's silence: its buffs count for nothing and its components' keywords are muted (a Rapid entry acts once, a Burn lays nothing, a Volatile bites nothing) through its next round, then wake; its stores fill and spend as ever. Can be cleansed; a Ward turns the silence away.

design.holes: Its stores are untouched (a lever if silence does not hurt enough); a store's active effect, when one exists, is a buff and sleeps with them.

table.stacks: No

entries.name: Guarded
entries.codex: Foe status, a core's. It takes no damage while its parts stand: all of them, or any, by the foe.

table.stacks: No

entries.name: Barrier
entries.codex: Machine status. The next blow a foe lands on this machine deals no damage, so it never injures; its riders land. Until the round's end. Never granted to every ally at once.

table.stacks: No
table.lasts: Until the next blow a foe lands on it, or the round's end

entries.name: Ward
entries.codex: Machine status. Every blow a foe lands on this machine this round leaves no rider (breach, burn, scorch, disable, corrupt), and no silence or purge touches it; its damage lands. Until the round's end.

design.holes: A foe's move that lays a debuff without a blow is no rider, so the Ward leaves it.

table.stacks: No

entries.name: Scorch
entries.codex: Foe attack keyword with a number. Each blow that lands leaves that many stacks of Scorched on the machine it hit (Scorch 2: two): its weapons and debuffs run hotter.

entries.name: Muster
entries.codex: Machine store, the Swallowtail's: a charge its locked pieces spend for their charged forms. Every die that rolls fills it a sliver, about thirty rolls a charge, and a kill by its own guns five rolls' worth; stored up to its cap. Starts each fight empty and never decays; a store, so no Silence or Purge touches it. With a charge up, its locked pieces go out charged unasked, unless the charged form has nowhere to land; then the plain form goes out and the charge waits.

design.holes: Every number is a placeholder; carrying it between fights is section 12's heat question.

table.stacks: Yes: a charge about thirty rolls of any die, five rolls' worth a kill by its guns, up to its cap

entries.name: Rallied
entries.codex: Machine status, the Swallowtail's Reveille Horn: its team has one reroll more this round.

design.holes: The reroll it grants counts toward the Muster when spent on the carrier: the intended combo, held by the cap.

table.stacks: No

entries.name: Regenerating
entries.codex: Machine status, the Storm Petrel's. It regains 2 shield at the start of each round for three rounds. Each grant keeps its own clock, so two grants regain 4 a round until the first runs out.

design.holes: Planned until the engine has a round-start shield on a timed status and the rider on a weapon's own spender. The number is a placeholder.

table.stacks: Yes: each grant its own clock

entries.name: Ammo
entries.codex: The Musk Ox's magazine, a bar under its heat bar, a notch an ammo. Its weapons spend ammo instead of heating it: 1 for every 2 heat a gun would make, rounded up, at least 1, the price printed where the gun's heat would be; a foe's Scorched still heats them. The magazine holds 10, opens each fight at 3 and gains 1 at the start of every round after the first; a vent the Musk Ox spends on itself adds 3, a shield 2. With too little left, a gun cannot be spent (DRY).

design.holes: Never a buff, so no Silence or Purge reaches it. If ammo runs plentiful, the vents' and shields' reloads or the trickle come down.
